summary: Daniel M. Neuman is an Indologist who studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago. He held posts at Dartmouth College (1971–1980), the University of Washington (1980–1995), and the University of California, Los Angeles (~1994–2018).

Daniel M. Stuart is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt. He held posts at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017) and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Daniel P. Brown was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Geshe Wangyal. He served as a professor at Harvard University from approximately 1980 to 2021.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his thesis at Florida State University, where he studied under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Schlumberger was a historian and archaeologist who specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1923–1925), succeeded Joseph Hackin, and held a post at Princeton University (~1969–1970).

Daniel Sperber is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Kilburn Grammar School, Kol Torah, Yeshivah of Flatbush, and University College London (~1965–1968), and held posts at Bar-Ilan University (~1968) and the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Stuart Capper is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA and MA at the University of Virginia, studying under Robert P. Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2000).

Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania. He studied under Parimal G. Patil, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.

Daniel Veidlinger works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as a research associate at Chiang Mai University (1999), and held a post at California State University, Chico (attested 2006).

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia. He held instructor posts at the University of Virginia (attested 2010) and Mary Baldwin University (attested 2010).
Daniela Berti is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Siena. She was attested as a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya in 2004.

Daniela Bevilacqua is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned PhDs from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University. She served as a post-doctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).
Daniele Cuneo held academic posts at the University of Paris and the Sorbonne (both attested 2018), and is attested as a faculty member at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.
Danielle Feller is an Indologist who earned her PhD from the University of Lausanne through 2001 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst. She also studied under Ganesh U. Thite.
Danping Long is an Indology and Buddhist studies researcher who is attested as a doctoral student at the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.
Danuta Stasik is an Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw (~1975–1980) under Maria Byrski (~1980–1989). She later held posts at the University of Warsaw, beginning in 1980 and 1986.

Daoquan Yu was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1934–1937). He served as a professor at Minzu University of China from approximately 1953 to 1992.

Dasharatha Sharma was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Delhi. He headed history at Hindu College, was Reader at Delhi (~1960–1969), Professor and Dean at Jai Narain Vyas (1966), and Director of Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (~1970–1976).

Daud Ali is an Indologist and historian educated at William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS University of London (~1995–2008) and became associate professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.
David A. Dilworth is a scholar in philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968).
